overview: Cytoplasm is everything inside the cell membrane except the nucleus; cytosol is just the fluid part of that.
genZNote: Cytoplasm is the whole room's contents. Cytosol is just the water filling the empty space.

aspects.label: Definition
aspects.valueA: All the material inside the plasma membrane, excluding the nucleus — includes organelles plus the fluid.
aspects.valueB: The semi-fluid, gel-like liquid component of the cytoplasm, excluding organelles.

aspects.label: Contents
aspects.valueA: Organelles (mitochondria, ER, Golgi, etc.) suspended within the cytosol.
aspects.valueB: Water, dissolved ions, small molecules, and soluble proteins — no organelles.

aspects.label: Relationship
aspects.valueA: The larger category — cytosol is one component of the cytoplasm.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Glycolysis occurs in the cytosol, not just 'the cytoplasm' loosely — precise wording matters in exams.
overlay.memoryTrick: Cytosol = just the 'sol' (solution/fluid) part of the cytoplasm.
overlay.commonMisconception: Cytoplasm and cytosol are often used interchangeably in casual speech, but strictly cytosol excludes the organelles that cytoplasm includes.
